children: Fitch Ratings said the US Treasury Department’s proposed restrictions on Banque Misr's (BM) five UAE branches are likely to have only a limited impact on the Egyptian lender's credit profile.

The proposed rule would prohibit US financial institutions from opening or maintaining US dollar correspondent accounts for, or on behalf of, Banque Misr UAE, significantly restricting the branches' access to US dollar banking services.
Fitch said the UAE branches make a limited contribution to Banque Misr's balance sheet and profitability, containing contagion risk to the bank's wider operations.

“However, we will assess the implications of the final outcome, including any reputational risks or an impact on BM’s ability to service its foreign-currency obligations,” the agency said in a recent report.

The rating agency added that the National Bank of Egypt's planned acquisition of Banque Misr's UAE branches, announced on September 22, could mitigate risks arising from the proposed restrictions, although details on the transaction remain undisclosed.

At end-2025, the UAE branches had US dollar-denominated obligations of $2.3 billion, representing 43% of their liabilities but only 2.5% of Banque Misr's total liabilities. Banque Misr's US dollar operations in other countries remain unaffected, Fitch said. The bank has appointed US legal counsel and plans to respond within the consultation period.

Meanwhile, with regard the planned IPO of Banque Misr’s majority owned subsidiary, Banque du Caire, analysts said the proposed sanctions on the lender’s UAE operations should not alter the investment case for Banque du Caire.
(Writing by Brinda Darasha; editing by Daniel Luiz)

title: US proposed sanction on Banque Misr UAE branches has limited ratings impact: Fitch
